question:
The path of a ray of light incident on an interface separating two transparent media is shown in the figure. The refractive index (n) of medium B with respect to medium A is given by:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/051a11418f21fa514bcd1ccce607e0dc7ab597c1698bd2d0e42e061643cf8cc1.png]
solution:
The correct answer is __**n > 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The refractive index (n) of a medium is a measure of how much the speed of light is reduced inside the medium compared to its speed in a vacuum.
 
• When light travels from a medium with a lower refractive index (such as air) to a medium with a higher refractive index (such as water), it bends towards the normal line at the interface.
 
• The condition n > 1 indicates that medium B is optically denser than medium A, causing the light ray to bend towards the normal.
 
• This bending is described by Snell's Law, which relates the angles and the refractive indices of the two media.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Snell's Law:**

 
 
• Snell's Law states that the ratio of the sine of the angle of incidence (θ₁) to the sine of the angle of refraction (θ₂) is constant for light passing between two given media. This is expressed as: n₁ * sin(θ₁) = n₂ * sin(θ₂).
 
• Here, n₁ and n₂ are the refractive indices of medium A and medium B, respectively.
 
 
 
• **Refractive Index:**
 
 
• The refractive index of a medium is defined as the ratio of the speed of light in a vacuum (c) to the speed of light in the medium (v), given by n = c/v.
 
• A higher refractive index indicates that light travels more slowly in the medium.
 
 
 
• **Optical Density:**
 
 
• Optical density is a measure of how much a medium can slow down light. A medium with a higher refractive index is considered optically denser.
 
• When light enters an optically denser medium, it slows down and bends towards the normal line.
 
 
 
• **Normal Line:**
 
 
• The normal line is an imaginary line perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence where the light ray hits the interface between two media.
 
• Light rays bend towards the normal when entering a denser medium and away from the normal when entering a less dense medium.
